thread:
maria.dev: heads-up — after flipping the FP8 kernels on H100 for the new 13B run, we're seeing small but consistent accuracy drift vs FP16 on our eval set (bleu/drop ~0.8-1.5%).
jonathan: ugh. is that across batch sizes or only certain sequences?
maria.dev: looks worst at batch sizes >= 8 and sequence lengths around 1k. short sequences (~128) look fine.
liam: could be tiling/fragmentation differences in the kernel path causing different accumulation order. any nondet logs?
maria.dev: enabled deterministic flags, still repros. here's the quick repro command I used:
```
export MODEL=redwood-13b-v2
python eval/quality_run.py --model $MODEL --device cuda --dtype fp8 --bsz 8 --maxlen 1024 --seed 42
```
jonathan: nice. what about L40S? same config?
maria.dev: L40S also shows delta but slightly smaller (0.6-1.0%). H100 seems larger (1.1-1.5%).
sophia: did we enable the mixed-precision shim that uses fp8 kernels + fp16 accumulation? there was a recent change to channel reorder in the FP8 kernel PR.
maria.dev: yes, the rollout used the new shim (PR #3421). i bisected to that commit and regression disappears if i revert kernel_enable flag.
liam: hmm maybe activation scaling / per-tensor quant params are being recomputed with different reduction order leading to small scale mismatch. need to compare scales logged per-layer.
anil: i slapped in extra logging to dump activation scales for 3 layers, small example attached below. looks like layer 7 scale differs by ~2-3%.
jonathan: 2-3% scale delta could cause the 1% bleu delta we see. Are we using per-channel or per-tensor scales for activations?
maria.dev: per-tensor for now. AWQ/GPTQ runs we did earlier used per-channel for weights. This is activations only.
sophia: can you paste the log snippet?
maria.dev: 
```
[fp8-activation-log] layer=7 step=120 scale_fp8=0.3124 scale_fp16_ref=0.3195
[fp8-activation-log] layer=7 step=121 scale_fp8=0.3109 scale_fp16_ref=0.3190
```
liam: that is suspicious — the fp16_ref path computes scales using max(abs(x)) across the tile, while the fp8 kernel uses a fused reduce that chunks differently. reduce precision/ordering differences can change the max.
jonathan: could also be affected by continuous batching behaviour: when we batch multiple requests the running max might see different prefixes. any perf differences when you force batch_size=1?
maria.dev: BS=1 -> delta falls to ~0.2% for H100. So batching amplification seems real.
anil: that aligns with tiling + accumulation order theory. i can try forcing a stable reduce (atomic max across full tensor) in the kernel for a test build.
sophia: also double-check kv-cache shape handling — we had a subtle pad vs ceil_div bug earlier that changed attention masks when tile padding used FP8 path. but that usually causes bigger regressions.
liam: worth running the eval with AWQ/GPTQ quantized variants to see if weight-only quantization masks this. if both weights and activations quantize differently, deltas might cancel or compound.
maria.dev: quick AWQ weight quant run (fp8 kernels for activations but AWQ weights) showed slightly better alignment: delta ~0.5% on H100. odd.
nathan: (infra-bot) new build 2026.03.08-fp8-exp deployed to canary pool; watch logs at https://ci.internal/redwood/builds/7342
jonathan: can we get a micro-benchmark that isolates the activation-scale compute? something that runs a single transformer block with deterministic rng and prints max(abs(x)) from both codepaths.
liam: i'll add a standalone test in runtime/tests/scale_consistency_test.cc — will run on both H100 and L40S.
anil: if it's ordering, we might mitigate by switching to fp16 accumulation for the scale reduction while keeping fp8 kernels for matmuls. that may cost a little perf but preserve quality.
sophia: decision call: roll back FP8 kernel rollout for broad traffic until we have scale-consistent fix/patch?
maria.dev: i'd prefer canary-only for now. rollback would hurt perf wins we're seeing for short-latency paths.
jonathan: canary-only + feature-flag default off for dedicated clusters seems reasonable. PR for flag revert + telemetry to capture per-layer scale distributions?
liam: creating PR to add a `--fp8-stable-reduce` flag and a telemetry path to record per-layer scale histograms. will attach patches.
anil: i'll prototype kernel change that computes the reduce in fp16 across the full tile (expensive) and compare. if match, we can optimize a mixed strategy.
sophia: also add regression tests to eval harness that assert BLEU/EM deltas < 0.5% vs FP16 baseline for canary models. If it flunks, auto-disable fp8 path in canary.
maria.dev: good, i'll open an issue with the eval artifacts and the failing prompt ids. putting the canary back on hold until liam's flag lands.
jonathan: thanks — let's sync tomorrow 10am to review kernels + telemetry. :thumbsup:
liam: pinged in PR description with traces and a tiny reproducer.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: canary pool paused for fp8-enabled runtime (reason: regression investigation)
